metadata.case_name: MAK PO LING v. YOUNG YAU YAU CECILIA

injuries.description: what is the particular dental condition of this patient is that she had six impacted teeth on her upper jaw.
source: If I move back to paragraph 5 of the Plaintiff’s witness statement, she complained about her pain and suffering during the whole period of the treatment. She said her upper teeth cannot fit comfortably with her lower teeth. She suffered from ulcer of gum, causing serious pain.

Paragraph 7 of this report said this: “The crucial issue is whether the Defendant had a proper and effective treatment plan to deal with the patient’s dental condition.” Now, what is the particular dental condition of this patient is that she had six impacted teeth on her upper jaw. So, it appears from this report that there must be special planning and that is one of the reasons that created the complication.

In the report of Dr Tong, he has this to say about the remedial treatment given by Dr Leung: On 10 September 2005, Dr Leung took record on Miss Mak and reassessed the case. He discovered that there were a total of six impacted teeth which Miss Mak had never been previously informed by Dr Young.

source: Three of my lower teeth were removed in the course of the orthodontic treatment. The lower left first bicuspid, (tooth 34), and the bridge pontic at tooth 45, (the lower right second bicuspid) were removed at the initial stage of the orthodontic treatment. The lower right first molar, (tooth 46) were later removed in March 2005.

manifestations.description: Upper teeth cannot fit comfortably with her lower teeth
ulcer of gum, causing serious pain
inarticulate and could not discharge her responsibility properly as a flight attendant, including but not limited to the making of announcements to passengers
serious loss of appetite and weight
wedding banquet has to be cancelled and unsatisfactory orthodontic condition has seriously lowered her self-esteem
lower jaw slides before coming to a halt when biting down (due to unstable occlusion and prematureocclusal contact)
Food get caught between teeth after eating (due to spacings between teeth)
unable to chew up food effectively and efficiently (due to poor occlusion)
teeth are sensitive to hot and cold (due to gingival recession, exposing roots of the teeth)
has to constantly restrain herself from showing her front teeth when laughing / loss of self-confidence with the present condition and appearance of her teeth
When the chewing force is not evenly distributed among all the teeth with the presence of an unstable occlusion and premature occlusal contact, the longevity of the affected teeth will be decreased.
Presence of spacing between teeth may lead to earlier deterioration of the periodontium (gum and bones) which supports the dentition.

treatments_received: Orthodontic treatment by the Defendant from June 2004 to June 2005
Remedial orthodontic treatment by Dr David Leung from September 2005 to February 2009 (41 months)
Removal of orthodontic appliance by Dr Leung
Upper removable retainer and lower free fixed retainer prescribed by Dr Leung
Extraction of three lower teeth during course of treatment (tooth 34, bridge pontic at tooth 45, tooth 46)
treatments_future: Option to restore or improve masticatory functions (as per Dr Tong)
Option to aim for optimum result (aesthetics and functions) (as per Dr Tong)
Possible future treatment costing in the range of $40,000 to $60,000 (Dr Tong's estimate)

losses.description: Extraction of three lower teeth and evidence of generalised root resorption and interproximal alveolar bone loss.

losses.category: Loss of ability to enjoy food and drink
losses.description: Unable to chew up food effectively and efficiently; has to cut food into small pieces and swallow without chewing; food gets caught between teeth; serious loss of appetite and weight.

losses.category: Loss of confidence in going out in the public
losses.description: Has lost her self-confidence with the present condition and appearance of her teeth; constantly restrains herself from showing her front teeth when laughing.
Unsatisfactory orthodontic condition affecting appearance of teeth leading to lowered self-esteem and social consequences (including cancellation of wedding banquet).
Psychological disturbance and/or depression as stated by the Plaintiff.
